profile.background: Cameron is 26 and labels incoming items in a museum storeroom. Cameron lives with a friend and has recently changed hours at work.
profile.history: Cameron has regular follow-up for schizophrenia. Speech is usually brief even with familiar people. Cameron has kept working with a modified schedule.
profile.guardedness: Willing to discuss work and home routines.
profile.self_understanding: Has noticed that a later start makes mornings easier.

facts.content: Checks the number on each incoming item and makes a matching paper label.
Received a replacement ID badge and a replacement locker key. The old badge cracked and was handed back. The old locker key was lost and could not be handed back. Neither replacement cost anything.
facts.disclosure_context: When asked about new work items.

facts.content: Clips the ID badge to a blue lanyard.
facts.disclosure_context: When discussing use of the badge.

facts.content: Takes the prescribed daily tablet with the evening meal.
Grows mint on the kitchen windowsill.
Usually gets roughly eight hours of sleep these days.
Walks to the museum with the friend who shares the flat.
facts.disclosure_context: When asked about the work commute.

facts.content: The work changes were shorter shifts and a later start. Cameron requested the later start. The supervisor suggested shorter shifts. Cameron would like to keep starting later if the schedule is reviewed.
facts.disclosure_context: When discussing the schedule or preferences.

dialogue.question: What do you do with an item when it first comes into the storeroom?
dialogue.answer: I check the number on it, then make a paper label with the same number.

dialogue.question: I see a replacement ID badge and locker key on your work checklist. Did you have to pay for the replacement?
dialogue.answer: No. They didn’t charge me for either the badge or the key.

dialogue.question: When do you take your tablet?
dialogue.answer: I take it with my evening meal.

dialogue.question: You had your badge and your locker key replaced. Did you hand the old one back?
dialogue.answer: I handed the old badge back. It had cracked. I’d lost the old key, so I couldn’t hand that back.

dialogue.question: Did you return the old ID badge when you got the replacement?
dialogue.answer: Yes, I handed it back. It had cracked.

dialogue.question: What do you clip the new one to?
dialogue.answer: I clip it to my blue lanyard.

dialogue.question: What do you grow on the kitchen windowsill?
How many hours of sleep do you usually get these days?
Who do you usually walk to the museum with?
dialogue.answer: With my friend who shares the flat.

dialogue.question: Your week changed in two ways, shorter shifts and a later start. Was that change something you asked for?
dialogue.answer: I asked for the later start. My supervisor suggested the shorter shifts. I’d like to keep starting later—it makes mornings easier.

dialogue.question: Were the shorter shifts your suggestion?
dialogue.answer: No, my supervisor suggested the shorter shifts. I asked for the later start.

dialogue.question: If work reviews the schedule again, what would you most like to keep?
dialogue.answer: I’d most like to keep the later start. It makes mornings easier.
